sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western edge of Union Beach, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. Ocean Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and Shore Road along the bottom, with Union Avenue crossing the sheet on a slight upward slant from left to right. Stone Road is lettered along the left margin, beside a dash-dot boundary line marked Raritan Township, and the cross streets from left to right are Washington Avenue, Aumack Avenue, Clark Avenue and Morningside Avenue at the right edge, where the sheet continues on sheet 3. The blocks north of Union Avenue are lettered B1, B6, B7 and B12 and are cut into narrow lots of about 25 feet, most of them vacant; the few buildings are scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small sheds and garages, with a cluster of dwellings near Stone Road and along Washington and Aumack Avenues. South of Union Avenue the blocks are lettered GG, FF, EE, NN, MM, LL and KK, and are almost empty of buildings. A miniature golf course is lettered in the lower left, below Union Avenue and west of Washington Avenue. Water pipes of 4, 5 and 6 inches are marked along the avenues, with hydrants at corners. Shore Road at the lower right is marked Not Open, as is part of Aumack Avenue south of Union Avenue and Washington Avenue south of Union. The sheet shows a thinly built subdivision on the western fringe of the borough in 1930, with the scale bar at the lower left and the Union Beach stamp at the upper right.
notes: The golf course is lettered Minature Golf Course on the sheet.
Stone Road has no junction with the listed streets in OpenStreetMap and is not used for control.
Fit: 12 detected junctions, RMSE 0.32 m, fitted scale 7.89 px/ft, rotation 94.1 degrees. Union Avenue and Shore Road at Washington Avenue are drawn narrower than the modern right-of-way.
50 ft. Stone Rd to Morningside Av, Ocean Av to Shore Rd. One part, 12 GCPs.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the centre of Union Beach west of the Central Railroad of New Jersey line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. Ocean Avenue runs along the top and Shore Road along the bottom, with Union Avenue crossing the sheet on a slight slant, rising towards the right. The cross streets from left to right are Morningside Avenue, Sydney Avenue, Cambridge Avenue, Jersey Avenue and, at the right edge, Columbia Avenue. North of Union Avenue the blocks are lettered B13, B18, B19 and B22; south of it they are lettered CC, BB, AA and H, with JJ, II and HH below Shore Road. Union Avenue is the commercial street: its blocks between Sydney and Jersey Avenues hold rows of stores, a large Tile Hall heated by steam and lit by electricity, and the Union Beach Fire Co. No. 1 Fire House at its corner, with a Dance Hall and a club on the south side near Sydney Avenue. Elsewhere the lots are narrow strips of about 25 feet with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, garages and sheds, many lots still empty. The Central Railroad of New Jersey is drawn as a pair of lines running up the page east of Jersey Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked along the avenues, with hydrants and a telephone house near Sydney Avenue. Edges of sheets 2, 4, 5 and 9 appear around the margins, and the scale bar and Union Beach stamp are at the right.
notes: Railroad is lettered C.R.R. of N.J.; it is a former line today (Henry Hudson Trail) and gives no control points.
Fit: 14 detected junctions, RMSE 0.38 m, fitted scale 7.92 px/ft, rotation 94.0 degrees.
50 ft. Morningside to Columbia Av, Ocean Av to Shore Rd, C.R.R. of N.J. at right. One part, 14 GCPs.

sheet-4-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 4, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. It covers the part of Union Beach between Columbia Avenue at the left and Bay View Avenue at the right, from Spruce along the top to Ocean Avenue along the bottom. Central Avenue, Park Avenue and Lorillard Avenue cross between them. West Creek, a tidal stream drawn in blue, crosses the middle of the sheet from the left edge to Lorillard Avenue; Park Avenue crosses it on a wooden bridge and the avenues to either side stop at the banks. The blocks north of the creek are lettered Q, P, I and H, and those south of it B24, B25, B28 and B29. All are cut into narrow lots of about 25 feet; nearly all of the lots are empty, and the buildings are scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with sheds, a few clustered near Columbia and Central Avenues, with a small tile building and a concrete block and tile structure near Ocean Avenue. A rectangle at the right, bounded by a heavy line, is the inset part 2, which shows the area beyond Bay View Avenue at Spruce and is not part of this mask. Bay View Avenue is marked Impassable along its southern length and Ocean Avenue is marked Not Open at its lower right end. Water pipes of 6 inches are marked along the avenues, with hydrants at corners. The adjoining sheets 3, 5, 9 and 16 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
The junction of Bay View and Ocean Avenues is not drawn (Bay View is Impassable and Ocean Not Open there) and is undetected.
Columbia Avenue does not meet Spruce Street in OpenStreetMap, so that corner is not used.
Fit: 8 detected junctions, RMSE 1.01 m, leave-one-out 1.88 m, fitted scale 7.98 px/ft, rotation 95.0 degrees.
Spruce is lettered without a suffix; it is Spruce Street in OpenStreetMap (reading corrected by the lead).
50 ft. Part 1 main (Columbia to Bay View Avs, Spruce to Ocean Av, West Creek); part 2 inset lower right (Spruce at Bay View and Prospect Avs), anchored on hand-picked junctions. North to the right.

sheet-4-2.description: Part 2 is an inset at the lower right of sheet 4, outlined by a heavy line and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with a compass arrow at its left edge. It continues the area north of the main map: Spruce runs along the top, where the number 16 refers to the adjoining sheet, and Bay View Avenue and Prospect Avenue run down the page at the left and right. The inset shows blocks of narrow lots of about 25 feet between them, laid out with their long sides parallel to Spruce. Buildings are scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with sheds, mostly clustered along Bay View and Prospect Avenues, and many lots are empty. All three streets are labelled 40 feet wide, with 6 inch water pipes along them and hydrants at the corners. The number 8 beside Prospect Avenue refers to sheet 8, which continues the area to the right. The inset repeats ground drawn in the main part of the sheet at Bay View Avenue but at a different position on the page, so it is a separately placed part.
notes: Placed from two hand-picked points 240 ft apart (Spruce Street at Bay View and at Prospect Avenues) with the scale and north taken from part 1, so low confidence; the second point agrees with the anchored fit to 0.96 m.
Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Spruce is lettered without a suffix; it is Spruce Street in OpenStreetMap (reading corrected by the lead).
50 ft. Part 1 main (Columbia to Bay View Avs, Spruce to Ocean Av, West Creek); part 2 inset lower right (Spruce at Bay View and Prospect Avs), anchored on hand-picked junctions. North to the right.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers four residential blocks in the centre of Union Beach, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. Ocean Avenue runs along the top of the sheet and Shore Road along the bottom, with Union Avenue crossing the middle on a slight slant; the cross streets, from left to right, are Columbia Avenue, Central Avenue, Park Avenue, Lorillard Avenue and Bay View Avenue. Blocks are lettered B23, B26, B27 and B30 north of Union Avenue and G, F, E and D south of it, and are cut into narrow numbered lots of about 25 feet. Most buildings are one- and two-storey frame dwellings with auto garages and sheds, many set back on otherwise empty lots, which shows a subdivision still being built up in 1930. A short commercial row of stores faces Union Avenue between Columbia and Park Avenues, including a drug store and several tile-walled stores, and a lumber storage building stands on Central Avenue south of Union Avenue. A Congregational church stands on the west side of Central Avenue in block B26, with a note on its heating and lighting. Two concrete-block garages stand in block B30. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 10 inches are drawn along the avenues, with hydrants at the corners. Bay View Avenue north of Union Avenue is marked as not open and impassable, and the stretch of Ocean Avenue at the upper right is also marked not open. Adjoining sheets 3, 4, 6, 7 and 8 are indicated around the margins.
notes: Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Bay View Avenue north of Union Avenue is marked Not Open and Impassable; Ocean Avenue at the upper right is marked Not Open.
Pilot sheet of the atlas: 13 detected junctions, fitted scale 7.91 px/ft.
50 ft. Columbia to Bay View Avs between Ocean Av, Union Av and Shore Rd. Pilot sheet. North to the right. One part.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the southern part of Union Beach around West Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. Shore Road runs across the top of the sheet. Jersey Avenue runs down the page at the left beside the Central Railroad of New Jersey line, and Central Avenue and Park Avenue run down from Shore Road through the middle. Below Shore Road the grid breaks into angled blocks: Beach View Avenue crosses from upper left to lower right and meets Central, Park and Lorillard Avenues, the last running diagonally up to the right edge. Sea View Avenue, also lettered with the alternative name X, runs parallel to it at the left, and Breeze Avenue, Water and Bay View Avenue lie further down the page. The angled blocks are cut into narrow lots of about 25 feet, and are lettered I, J, K, T, U and V; dwellings and sheds stand mostly along Beach View Avenue and the upper blocks, while the lower blocks near the creek are empty. West Creek, drawn in blue, winds from the left edge down to the lower right and crosses several paper streets. Harris Avenue is lettered at the bottom left, and a street at the left is marked Not Named. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches run along the main avenues, with hydrants at corners. The Union Beach stamp is at the upper right and the neighbouring sheets 3, 8, 9 and 5 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Beach View Avenue is Beachview Avenue and Sea View Avenue is Seaview Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue.
Breeze Avenue and Water are not in OpenStreetMap as named streets.
Sea View Avenue is lettered X. or Sea View Av.; the X is read as printed.
A street at the lower left is lettered Not Named; the railroad at the left is lettered C.R.R. of N.J. (former line, no control points).

Placed from 6 detected junctions and 3 hand-picked pipe and street-centre junctions (Jersey Avenue and Lorillard Avenue at Shore Road, Central Avenue at Sea View Avenue). Fit: RMSE 0.26 m, leave-one-out 0.39 m, 7.96 px/ft, rotation 94.2 degrees. Beach View Avenue meets Park and Lorillard Avenues within 8 m of one another.
50 ft. Jersey Av to Bay View Av, Shore Rd down to Harris Av, angled blocks and West Creek; Sea View Av, Beach View Av, Breeze Av, Water. One part.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the eastern side of Union Beach and the line of West Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. Ocean Avenue runs along the top and Shore Road along the bottom; Union Avenue crosses the middle on a slight upward slant to the right. Bay View Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Brook Avenue run down the page from left to right. West of the creek the blocks are lettered B31, B34, C and B, and are laid out as long narrow lots of about 25 feet; the area north of Union Avenue is nearly empty, with a few dwellings along Union Avenue, and the blocks south of it hold a loose scatter of one- and two-storey frame dwellings with sheds. Ocean Avenue is marked Not Open, and Bay View Avenue is marked Impassable. West Creek, drawn in blue, comes in from the top and bends down to the lower right, crossing Union Avenue on a wooden bridge. East of the creek the street plan turns: Front is lettered along a diagonal street running down beside the creek, with fan-shaped blocks lettered A, and a small block of 2nd Street and Cedar at the upper right where they meet Union Avenue, with the number 14 pointing to sheet 14. The numbers 60 and 519 mark lots east of the creek. Water pipes of 6 and 10 inches run along the avenues, with hydrants at the corners. Sheets 4, 6, 8 and 14 are numbered at the margins.
notes: Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Front, Cedar and 2nd Street are not used for control: the OpenStreetMap Front Street at Union Avenue does not match them confidently.
Ocean Avenue at Bay View Avenue is not drawn through (Ocean Avenue marked Not Open) and was not detected.
Fit: 6 detected junctions, RMSE 0.71 m, leave-one-out 1.66 m, 7.93 px/ft, rotation 94.4 degrees. Control lies west of the creek; the area east of it (Front, Cedar) is extrapolated.
50 ft. Bay View to Brook Av, Ocean Av to Shore Rd, West Creek; Front and Cedar and 2nd St east of the creek (no control there, extrapolated). One part.

sheet-8-1.description: Part 1 is the main map of sheet 8, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the right. It covers the southeastern streets of Union Beach between Shore Road along the top and the lower edge of the sheet. Below Shore Road the streets run straight down the page for about a block and then turn into a fan: Lorillard Avenue, Bay View Avenue, Prospect Avenue and Brook Avenue bend towards the lower left, and Front is lettered on the diagonal street at the right edge. Beach View Avenue crosses them from upper left to lower right near the middle of the sheet, and Breeze Avenue is lettered at the lower left. The angled blocks are cut into long narrow lots of about 25 feet, lettered K, M, N, O, P and Q; dwellings and sheds stand mostly in the blocks near Shore Road and along Lorillard Avenue, and the lower blocks are empty. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches follow the avenues, with hydrants at the corners. The upper margin carries the numbers 5 and 7 for the adjoining sheets and a compass arrow at the upper left, with 6 at the left edge and 16 and 4 at the inset to the lower right. A rectangle at the lower right, outlined by a heavy line, is a separate inset (part 2) and is not part of this mask. The scale bar and the Union Beach stamp, dated July 1930, are at the bottom and upper right.
notes: Bay View, Beach View and Prospect Avenues are Bayview, Beachview and Prospect Avenues in OpenStreetMap.
Breeze Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap as a named street.

Lorillard Avenue is drawn 25 ft wide against 40 ft in the parcels, and its junction with Beach View Avenue (detected 3 to 5 m off the fit) was left out. The Lorillard Avenue junction with Shore Road is hand-picked at the crossing of the drawn pipes.

Fit: 5 control points (4 along Shore Road plus Bay View and Beach View Avenues); RMSE 0.08 m but the points are nearly collinear, so rotation and scale rest on one far point; low confidence in the lower part of the sheet.

50 ft. Part 1 main (Shore Rd, Lorillard to Brook and Front, fan blocks, Beach View and Breeze Avs; modern streets south of Beach View are gone, placement checked against parcels); part 2 inset lower right (Spruce at Prospect St), anchored.

sheet-8-2.description: Part 2 is an inset at the lower right of sheet 8, outlined by a heavy line on its left and upper sides and drawn at 50 feet to an inch. It continues the area shown in the inset of sheet 4, north of Spruce Street. Spruce is lettered along the top of the inset, with the number 16 above it pointing to sheet 16, and Prospect St. runs down the page at the left beside the heavy line, with a 6 inch water pipe and a hydrant. Both streets are marked 40 feet wide. To the right of Prospect Street the inset shows a block of long narrow lots of about 25 feet, numbered in the 200s, with a few frame dwellings and sheds in the lower part; the upper part is empty. The number 4 beside the heavy line at the left refers to sheet 4 and a compass arrow appears at the right edge. The inset overlaps ground drawn in the main part of the sheet, but at a different position on the page, and is a separately placed part.
notes: Prospect St. is Prospect Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from one measured junction (Spruce Street at Prospect Avenue) with scale 7.95 px/ft and north from the config, so low confidence. The same junction is drawn in the inset of sheet 4 (part 2), which was placed independently.

50 ft. Part 1 main (Shore Rd, Lorillard to Brook and Front, fan blocks, Beach View and Breeze Avs; modern streets south of Beach View are gone, placement checked against parcels); part 2 inset lower right (Spruce at Prospect St), anchored.

sheet-9-1.description: The lower part of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the right, covers the south-western corner of Union Beach below Shore Road, separated from the upper part of the sheet by a heavy line. Stone Road runs down the left edge along the borough limits, with Raritan Township beyond it. Washington, Aumack, Clark, Morningside, Sydney and Cambridge Avenues run from the top edge (blocks NN to HH, the south side of the blocks on sheets 2 and 3) down to West Creek, which winds across the part from left to right. South of the creek a newer subdivision is laid out on a slant: High Avenue, Harris Avenue and Patterson Avenue cross Isabelle Avenue, Willow, Asbury and Cambridge Avenues, and a road fronting on Hill Avenue runs along the bottom edge. Jersey Avenue runs down the right side beside the double track of the C.R.R. of N.J., with a short unnamed street, Water Street and Beach View Avenue beyond the railroad. Most of the part is platted lots with few buildings: scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, sheds and garages, an auto repair shop and the Harris Gardens Hose Co. on Stone Road, a cement block manufacturing building near Stone Road and Isabelle Avenue, and a row of small dwellings and tile buildings near Jersey Avenue. Block letters A to R mark the blocks south of the creek. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches run along Stone Road, Isabelle Avenue, High Avenue, Harris Avenue and Jersey Avenue. The sheet's scale bar, at 100 feet to an inch, is printed at the bottom of this part.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, unlike most sheets of the atlas (50 feet).
Isabelle Avenue appears in OpenStreetMap as both Isabelle Avenue and Isabella Avenue; Willow is Willow Street and Asbury is Asbury Avenue.
The C.R.R. of N.J. along Jersey Avenue is not a running line in OpenStreetMap; its former line is the Henry Hudson Trail.
Hill Avenue is lettered only as 'Fronting on Hill Av.' along the bottom edge.
Borough limits with Raritan Township (now Hazlet) are marked along Stone Road.

100 ft (scale bar). Part 1 (lower): Stone Rd to Jersey Av south of Shore Rd, West Creek, High, Harris and Patterson Avs, Isabelle Av, Willow, Asbury. Part 2 (upper): Stone Rd to Columbia Av between Ocean Av and Spruce St (Sea Gate), water tank. Split by a heavy line. North to the right.

sheet-9-2.description: The upper part of sheet 9, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the right, covers the western end of Union Beach between Ocean Avenue at the bottom and Spruce Street beyond the top edge. Stone Road runs along the left edge on the borough limits, with Raritan Township beyond. The avenues running up the page are, from left to right, Washington, Aumack, Clark, Morningside, Sydney, Cambridge, Jersey and Columbia Avenues, and Sea Gate crosses the middle of the part; blocks B2 to B21 are cut into narrow numbered lots. West Creek runs across the top of the part, with a wooden bridge where it passes under Morningside Avenue, and reappears at the right beside Columbia Avenue, where the ground east of the railroad is marked swamp. The double track of the C.R.R. of N.J. runs up the right side between Jersey and Columbia Avenues. Building is sparse and almost entirely residential: one- and two-storey frame dwellings, garages and sheds scattered over largely empty lots. All Souls R.C. Church, of concrete block, stands on Stone Road in block B3, with an auto repair garage nearby, and a machine shop stands in block B10. A 200,000 gallon water tank 127 feet high stands in block B11 near Ocean Avenue, fed by a 12 inch water pipe along Ocean Avenue; 4, 6 and 10 inch pipes run along the other avenues. A few tile-walled dwellings stand on Cambridge Avenue in block B20.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch, unlike most sheets of the atlas (50 feet).
Sea Gate is lettered without a suffix; it is Sea Gate Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Spruce Street is lettered only in the upper margin as the street beyond the top edge.
The water tank (200,000 gallons, 127 feet high) stands in block B11.
The C.R.R. of N.J. between Jersey and Columbia Avenues is not a running line in OpenStreetMap; its former line is the Henry Hudson Trail.

100 ft (scale bar). Part 1 (lower): Stone Rd to Jersey Av south of Shore Rd, West Creek, High, Harris and Patterson Avs, Isabelle Av, Willow, Asbury. Part 2 (upper): Stone Rd to Columbia Av between Ocean Av and Spruce St (Sea Gate), water tank. Split by a heavy line. North to the right.

sheet-10-1.description: The main part of sheet 10, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, covers the northern corner of Union Beach next to Keyport. Bay Avenue and Edmunds Avenue run up the page, crossed by Chingarora Street along the top edge, then Raritan, Henry, Herbert and Campbell Streets and Florence Avenue at the bottom; blocks Y, U, Q, M and I between Bay and Edmunds Avenues are cut into narrow numbered lots. In the lower left, separated from the inset above by a heavy line, the street pattern turns: St. Johns Avenue runs diagonally from State Street down to Florence Avenue, and W. Venice Place and E. Venice Place, both marked not open, flank a narrow drawn water way that ends at Campbell Street; blocks N, O, K, J and S lie here. The part is almost wholly residential, with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, auto garages and a few tile-walled garages spread thinly over the lots, many of which are empty. The largest building is Public School No. 1, a brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, at the corner of Florence Avenue and Edmunds Avenue in block I; next to it, on Bay Avenue, is a row of tile-walled stores and flats. Six-inch water pipes run along every street, with a 10 inch main in Florence Avenue, and hydrants stand at most corners. Sheets 11 and 16 adjoin on the right and at the bottom.
notes: Raritan, Henry, Herbert and Campbell are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Raritan Street, Henry Street, Herbert Street and Campbell Street, and Florence is Florence Avenue.
St. Johns Avenue is Saint Johns Avenue / St John's Avenue in OpenStreetMap; W. and E. Venice Place and the water way between them are not in OpenStreetMap.
Florence Avenue / St John's Avenue / Victoria Place was detected but rejected at 10 m from the fit: the modern junction has probably moved.
Public School No. 1 stands at Florence Avenue and Edmunds Avenue.

50 ft. Part 1 (main): Bay Av / Edmunds Av, Chingarora St to Florence Av; St Johns Av, State St, W and E Venice Pl (lower left). Part 2 (inset upper left): Florence Av at Broadway with the Samuel Rothstein Clothing Co., Borough water works, Jersey Central Power & Light sub-station, C.R.R. of N.J.; anchored on Broadway / Florence Av. North to the upper right.

sheet-10-2.description: The inset in the upper left of sheet 10, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and at the same orientation as the main part (north toward the upper right), shows the industrial ground south of Florence Avenue where Broadway meets it, on the western edge of Union Beach toward Keyport. Florence Avenue crosses the top of the inset with Broadway ending against it from the upper left; numbered parcels 502, 503 and 504 fill the rest, and the double track of the C.R.R. of N.J. crosses the lower left corner. The largest building is a long pilastered brick factory set diagonally to the street, occupied by the Samuel Rothstein Clothing Co. Inc. (heated by steam, with electric light and power and a watchman), with a club room at its northern end; its southern end houses the Borough of Union Beach Water Works filter room, with a fuel oil tank beside it. A long vacant frame building stands parallel to it nearer Florence Avenue. Toward the bottom of the inset is the Jersey Central Power & Light Co. electric sub-station, two brick buildings with raised floors, operating continuously. On the north side of Florence Avenue are a tile-walled store, a tile dwelling and two old and vacant sheds, with gasoline tanks near Broadway. Water mains of 8 and 12 inches run along Florence Avenue and across the site to the factory.
notes: Florence is Florence Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Broadway keeps its name.

Placed from the one junction Broadway / Florence Avenue with the scale of the main part (7.95 px/ft) and the rotation measured from the drawn street lines (45.7 degrees, the main part's is 46.0): low confidence.
The C.R.R. of N.J. line drawn here is not a running line in OpenStreetMap (its former line is the Henry Hudson Trail).

50 ft. Part 1 (main): Bay Av / Edmunds Av, Chingarora St to Florence Av; St Johns Av, State St, W and E Venice Pl (lower left). Part 2 (inset upper left): Florence Av at Broadway with the Samuel Rothstein Clothing Co., Borough water works, Jersey Central Power & Light sub-station, C.R.R. of N.J.; anchored on Broadway / Florence Av. North to the upper right.

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 lies in the northern part of Union Beach, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, the same turned orientation as the neighbouring sheets 10 and 12. Edmunds Avenue runs down the left side of the page, with Poole Avenue meeting it as a diagonal from the lower left, and 10th Street and 9th Street cross the sheet near its right edge. Herbert, Campbell and Florence run across the page, followed by Floyd Avenue, St. James Avenue and, along the bottom edge, Bay View Avenue, which is marked not open. Pine Street cuts diagonally across the lower right corner, with Bay View Avenue ending against it. The blocks are cut into long narrow lots numbered in the 100s and 200s, and most are empty. The buildings are scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small garages, a few tile or concrete-walled dwellings in the Florence Avenue blocks, and one blue-coloured building near the right edge. Grace M. E. Church stands on the north side of St. James Avenue in the lower left, heated by steam and lit by electricity. A long oblique property line crosses the middle of the sheet from the upper right toward the lower left. Water pipes of 6 inches run along the streets, with hydrants at the corners; the compass rose is at the upper left and the Union Beach stamp at the upper right. Sheet numbers 10, 12, 15 and 16 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Herbert, Campbell and Florence are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Herbert Street, Campbell Street and Florence Avenue. Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue and St. James Avenue is Saint James Avenue.
10th Street / Saint James Avenue was detected 7.7 m from the fit and rejected: the modern junction has probably moved.
9th Street / Campbell Street was measured from a narrow pair of edges (Campbell Street 26 of 50 ft).
Bay View Avenue is marked not open on the sheet.
50 ft. Herbert St to Bay View Av, Edmunds Av, 10th and 9th Sts, Floyd Av, St James Av, Grace M.E. Church. North to the upper right (rotation about 46). One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the blocks east of sheet 11 in the northern half of Union Beach, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Five numbered streets, 9th, 8th, 7th, 6th and 5th, run down the page; Herbert crosses the top, Florence the middle and Pine the bottom edge. Herbert is lettered not open, and the 9th Street margin and the 5th Street line at the upper right are also marked not open. Dock Street runs obliquely across the upper right from Florence Avenue toward the corner of the sheet, bordered on its north side by narrow lots at an angle to the grid (blocks 28, 34 and 50), where a few dwellings and a small building marked auto printing stand. The remaining blocks (34, 40, 46 above Florence and 35, 37, 41, 47 below it) are laid out in long narrow lots numbered in the 100s to 300s. The buildings are mostly one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, concentrated below Florence Avenue and along 8th and 6th Streets; the upper blocks are largely empty. A 10 inch water main runs in Florence Avenue and 6 inch pipes in the other streets, with hydrants at the corners. The compass rose and Union Beach stamp are in the upper right and the scale bar at the bottom right. Sheet numbers 11, 13 and 15 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Herbert, Florence and Pine are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Oak Street (the drawn Herbert, whose junctions with 9th, 8th and 7th Streets fit the modern Oak Street), Florence Avenue and Pine Street.
5th Street / Dock Street was measured at 2.0 m from the fit and 5th Street / Pine Street at 1.5 m.
Herbert is marked not open and was drawn as a paper street; the match with the modern Oak Street rests on the detector's fit to the lot lines.
50 ft. 9th to 5th Sts, Herbert (today Oak Street) to Pine. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 continues Sheet 12 toward the northeast along the bay side of Union Beach, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Florence Avenue crosses the middle of the page, Pine runs along the bottom edge and Beach along the top. The numbered streets 5th, Center, 4th, 3rd and 2nd run down the page; 4th Street is marked not open above Florence Avenue, and Beach and the upper part of 2nd Street are also marked not open. Dock Street crosses the upper left on a diagonal, with narrow lots on both sides set at an angle to the grid (blocks 5, 22, 23, 28 and 51 north of Florence Avenue), and the compass rose sits against Dock Street at the left. Blocks 10, 11, 17, 12, 18, 24 and 29 are cut into long narrow lots, most of them empty; the buildings are one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, several tile or concrete-walled dwellings in pink, and a few small stores or sheds near Dock Street. A 10 inch water main runs in Florence Avenue and 6 inch pipes in the other streets, with hydrants at the corners. The Union Beach stamp is at the top right and the scale bar at the bottom right. Sheets 12, 14 and 15 adjoin.
notes: Beach, Florence, Pine and Center are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Beach Street, Florence Avenue, Pine Street and Center Street.
2nd Street / Beach Street was detected 2.8 m from the fit and measured from a narrow pair (Beach Street 34 of 60 ft); Beach Street is marked not open.
5th Street / Dock Street, 3rd Street / Beach Street and 3rd Street / Dock Street were not detected (the last is 43 ft off the sheet).
50 ft. 5th to 2nd Sts, Beach to Pine, Dock, Center. One part.

sheet-14-1.description: The right-hand column of sheet 14, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right and separated from the left column by a heavy line, covers the southern half of the bay-shore strip of Union Beach between Pine at the top and Cedar at the bottom, continuing the strip drawn in the left column. 2nd Street runs down the left side and Front down the middle, with Spruce crossing between them; blocks 6, 7 and 8 between 2nd Street and Front are cut into long narrow lots and are almost empty apart from a store, a storage building and a few dwellings along Pine. East of Front, blocks 2 and 3 run out to the shore of Raritan Bay, drawn as a blue band on the right, with bathhouses, a tile-walled building and several frame dwellings and stores scattered along Front. Water pipes run along Pine, 2nd Street and Front, with hydrants at the corners. The sheet's compass rose stands on the dividing line and the scale bar at the lower right.
notes: Pine and Front are Pine Street and Front Street in OpenStreetMap; Spruce and Cedar do not reach 2nd Street or Front Street today.

Placed from 2nd Street / Pine Street with the atlas scale and the rotation measured from its drawn lines (45.5 degrees); the second junction on Pine, Front Street / Pine Street, lies 0.3 m from that placement. Low to medium confidence: the control is on the top edge only.
This column was first configured together with the left column as one part; it is a separate stretch of the shore and was split off by the lead.

50 ft. Two columns of the bay-shore strip split by a heavy line: part 1 right column (2nd St to the bay, Pine to Cedar), anchored on 2nd St / Pine St; part 2 left column (2nd St to the bay, Beach to Florence, Skee-Ball, carousel).

sheet-14-2.description: The left-hand column of sheet 14, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, covers the northern half of the bay-shore strip of Union Beach between Beach at the top and Florence in the lower third, with blocks continuing below toward Pine on the next column. 2nd Street and Front run down the page; Beach is marked not open. Blocks 4, 5 and 6 between them are cut into long narrow lots with a scatter of frame dwellings and garages, most in the lower part, and a tile-walled building. East of Front a strip of narrow lots along the shore holds the beach amusements: a Skee-Ball building, a carousel and a row of small one-storey concession stands, beside Raritan Bay, drawn as a blue band along the right edge of the column. Water pipes run along Beach, Florence, 2nd Street and Front.
notes: Beach, Florence and Front are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Beach Street, Florence Avenue and Front Street.
Beach is marked Not Open.
Fitted from four junctions (2nd Street and Front Street at Beach Street and Florence Avenue).

50 ft. Two columns of the bay-shore strip split by a heavy line: part 1 right column (2nd St to the bay, Pine to Cedar), anchored on 2nd St / Pine St; part 2 left column (2nd St to the bay, Beach to Florence, Skee-Ball, carousel).

sheet-15-1.description: The upper part of sheet 15, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, is a strip south of Pine Street that runs from the west edge of the district toward the shore. Pine is lettered along the top, with 9th, 8th, 7th, 6th and 5th Streets crossing it, and Spruce, marked not open, closes the blocks at the bottom. At the upper left Pine turns on a diagonal and meets Bay View Avenue, and Prospect runs obliquely across the left side from the upper left, with a fan of narrow wedge-shaped lots (block A) beside it and a few dwellings on the lots to its north. The remaining blocks (36, 42, 43 and 48) are laid out in long narrow lots numbered in the 100s and 300s; most are empty, with scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a garage or two and small tile buildings in pink. A heavy line along the bottom divides this part from the lower strip. The compass rose stands at the lower left, the Union Beach stamp at the upper right and 6 inch water pipes run in most streets, with hydrants at the corners. Sheets 11, 12 and 16 are indicated at the margins.
notes: Pine and Spruce are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Pine Street and Spruce Street. Prospect is Prospect Avenue and Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue.
Spruce Street is marked not open between 6th and 5th Streets.
Sheet 15 has two parts split by a heavy line: this upper strip and the lower strip, which continues east (5th to 2nd Streets).
50 ft. Two strips split by a heavy line: part 1 upper (9th to 5th Sts between Pine and Spruce), part 2 lower (5th to 2nd Sts between Pine and Spruce).

sheet-15-2.description: The lower part of sheet 15, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right, continues the strip south of Pine Street eastward from the upper part and is divided from it by a heavy line. Pine runs along the top and Spruce along the bottom, and 5th, Center, 4th, 3rd and 2nd Streets cross between them; 4th Street is marked not open in its lower half and Spruce at the bottom is marked not open too. Blocks 30, 25, 19 and 13 are cut into long narrow lots, numbered in the 100s to 500s, and the buildings are one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, clustered in the blocks along 5th Street and Center Street and scattered in the others; the blocks near 4th and 2nd Streets are mostly empty. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes run along the streets, with hydrants at corners, and a 33 foot street width is noted at several corners. The scale bar and the Union Beach stamp lie in the bottom right and the compass rose belongs to the upper part. Sheets 13 and 14 are indicated at the right margin and sheet 15 at the left.
notes: Pine, Spruce and Center are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Pine Street, Spruce Street and Center Street.
Sheet 15 has two parts split by a heavy line: this is the lower strip, 5th to 2nd Streets, and the upper strip covers 9th to 5th Streets.
50 ft. Two strips split by a heavy line: part 1 upper (9th to 5th Sts between Pine and Spruce), part 2 lower (5th to 2nd Sts between Pine and Spruce).

sheet-16-1.description: The main part of sheet 16, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north to the right, covers the north-western quarter of Union Beach (the Union Gardens section) from Poole Avenue and the creek at the top down to Spruce Street at the bottom. The double track of the C.R.R. of N.J. runs straight down the left third of the sheet, with the Union Beach R.R. station at its lower end beside Columbia Avenue; west of it Morningside Avenue and Sydney Avenue run diagonally through large unbuilt parcels numbered 504 to 513, with a short row of dwellings on a road along the creek at the upper left. East of the railroad the grid is formed by Columbia, Central, Park, Lorillard, Bay View and Prospect Avenues crossed by Poole Avenue, Maple, Pine, Wilson and Spruce; in the upper right the streets turn to meet Florence Avenue, with Victoria Place, James Avenue, Edmunds Avenue, Floyd Avenue and Bay Avenue, and 10th and 7th Streets touch the right edge. Blocks lettered A to U are cut into numbered lots, most holding one- and two-storey frame dwellings with garages, many still empty. Public buildings include the fire house of Union Hose Co. No. 1 on Florence Avenue in block B and the Union Gardens Fire Co. No. 1 on Central Avenue in block N; an auto repair garage stands on Poole Avenue, a vending stand and a printing shop on Bay View Avenue, and there is a concrete-block garage in block O. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 10 inches run along the main streets. Bay View Avenue north of Pine is marked not open.
notes: Drawn at 100 feet to an inch (scale bar on the sheet), unlike most sheets of the atlas (50 feet).

Poole, Maple, Pine, Wilson and Spruce are lettered without a suffix; in OpenStreetMap they are Poole Avenue, Maple Street, Pine Street, Wilson Avenue and Spruce Street. Bay View Avenue is Bayview Avenue, James Avenue is Saint James Avenue, Florence is Florence Avenue.
The C.R.R. of N.J. and the Union Beach R.R. station are not in OpenStreetMap as a running line; the former line is the Henry Hudson Trail.
Junctions around Florence Avenue at Poole and Edmunds Avenues and Poole / Sydney Avenue were detected 8 to 11 m from the fit and rejected: the modern streets there have probably been realigned.
Fire houses: Union Hose Co. No. 1 (Florence Avenue) and Union Gardens Fire Co. No. 1 (Central Avenue).

100 ft (scale bar). Part 1 (main): Poole Av to Spruce St, Morningside to Prospect Avs, C.R.R. of N.J. and Union Beach station, Victoria Pl, Florence Av. Part 2 (inset lower left): Morningside and Sydney Avs at Spruce St with Public School No. 2, continuing the main part past match points A-B; anchored on Morningside Av / Spruce St.

sheet-16-2.description: The inset in the lower left corner of sheet 16, boxed by a heavy line and drawn at 100 feet to an inch at the same orientation as the main part, continues Morningside Avenue and Sydney Avenue south-west of the edge of the main part (match points A and B are marked on both) down to Spruce Street. It shows parcel 512 between the two avenues, with Public School No. 2, a brick building heated by steam and lit by electricity, standing in it near Spruce Street; parcels 510, 513 and 525 lie around it. A note on Spruce Street gives the distance of 710 feet to the railroad station. Across Morningside Avenue are two small vending stands, and two dwellings stand south of Spruce Street near the edge of the inset. Water pipes of 6, 8 and 10 inches run along Morningside Avenue, Sydney Avenue and Spruce Street, with a hydrant at the Morningside Avenue corner.
notes: Spruce is Spruce Street in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from the single junction Morningside Avenue / Spruce Street, with the scale of the main part (3.98 px/ft) and the rotation measured from its drawn street lines (95.7 degrees, main part 95.9): low confidence.
Sydney Avenue does not reach Spruce Street in OpenStreetMap.
Public School No. 2 stands on Spruce Street between Morningside and Sydney Avenues.

100 ft (scale bar). Part 1 (main): Poole Av to Spruce St, Morningside to Prospect Avs, C.R.R. of N.J. and Union Beach station, Victoria Pl, Florence Av. Part 2 (inset lower left): Morningside and Sydney Avs at Spruce St with Public School No. 2, continuing the main part past match points A-B; anchored on Morningside Av / Spruce St.

sheet-17-1.description: The main part of sheet 17, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north approximately up the page (unlike the other sheets of the atlas), shows the Lorillard plant of the National Fireproofing Co., makers of building tile, on the eastern edge of the town, and Natco Road below it. The plant occupies the upper part of the sheet: a large brick block of drying tunnels with storage rooms, a moulding room, boiler house, engine room and a long mixing building, surrounded by a ring of round kilns to the north and west, with a separate office, a time office, a hay storage building and an oil house nearby, all built of fireproof construction with tile walls. A note records the watchman and clock, steam heat, electric light, fire pails, extinguishers and hose, and that no data was available on the water system. Two rail sidings curve into the plant from the left. Across the lower part of the sheet runs the double track of the C.R.R. of N.J. with a siding and Natco Station. Natco Road, 50 feet wide, runs south from the railroad at the lower left, lined on its west side by a row of tile-walled and frame company dwellings with garages on lots 26 to 39, with one more dwelling and a tile garage on its east side; the surrounding land is lettered L. The lower right corner belongs to an inset continuing Natco Road.
notes: Natco Road is identified with today's Rose Lane: the modern parcels along Rose Lane match the drawn lots and houses when the part is placed this way.
The C.R.R. of N.J. line is the former line now used by the Henry Hudson Trail; there is no running railroad in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from one hand-picked point (Natco Road at the C.R.R. of N.J. main track, taken as Rose Lane at the Henry Hudson Trail) with the atlas scale and a rotation of 7 degrees chosen so that the modern parcels match the drawn lots; the compass on the sheet points about 5 degrees left of up (probably magnetic north). Low confidence.
Sheet drawn with north approximately up, about 90 degrees from the other sheets of the atlas.

50 ft. North approximately up (about 90 degrees from the other sheets). Part 1: National Fireproofing Co. Lorillard Plant, C.R.R. of N.J. with Natco Station, Natco Road (today Rose Lane) with company houses; part 2 (inset lower right): Natco Road further south, overlapping part 1. Both placed from one point each (anchored, low confidence), checked against modern parcels.

sheet-17-2.description: The inset in the lower right of sheet 17, boxed by a heavy line and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north approximately up, continues Natco Road southward from the main part of the sheet. It shows a row of five two-storey frame company dwellings with rear wings on the west side of the road, on lots numbered 18 to 25, with small garages behind them, on land lettered L; the road is 50 feet wide, and the name of the National Fireproofing Co. Lorillard Plant is lettered along it, marking these as the company's houses. The two northernmost dwellings repeat the two southernmost ones drawn on the main part, so the inset overlaps the main part on the ground. The sheet's compass rose stands at the top of the inset and the scale bar, 50 feet to an inch, at its lower right.
notes: Natco Road is identified with today's Rose Lane.

Placed from one point carried from the main part of the sheet (the front corner of the dwelling on lots 24 and 25, drawn on both) with the atlas scale and the main part's rotation of 7 degrees; the modern parcels along Rose Lane match the drawn lots. Low confidence.

50 ft. North approximately up (about 90 degrees from the other sheets). Part 1: National Fireproofing Co. Lorillard Plant, C.R.R. of N.J. with Natco Station, Natco Road (today Rose Lane) with company houses; part 2 (inset lower right): Natco Road further south, overlapping part 1.
